subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys that look like credentials be allowed into skill-owned host `exec` subprocesses, and how should that interact with generic exec secret stripping?
rationale: The current code violates the documented host skill-env behavior for real users, but a broad allow-all change decides when credential values enter executable child processes and overlaps the open generic exec secret-leak hardening work.

options.title: Allow skill-scoped exec env
options.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

options.title: Require metadata declarations
options.body: Keep credential-shaped names blocked unless the skill manifest declares them, then update the `gog` skill metadata or package docs for this credential path.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Document that credential-shaped per-skill env names are intentionally blocked and require top-level, system, or sandbox-specific env configuration.

recommendation.title: Allow skill-scoped exec env
recommendation.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses documented skill behavior, credential filtering, and executable child-process policy where steipete has direct security-env history.
